thesis: After the preceding verses' pressure to bend revelation and expel the Messenger, Allah answers with regimen: prayer that holds the arc of the day, a fajr recitation that is divinely witnessed, and a portion of the night given to tahajjud that opens onto a praised station granted by the Lord.
notes: Ahkam adab holds cleanly. This file touches prayer timings and the maqam mahmud and stays on the tadabbur side of the line throughout: it never states when a prayer legally begins or ends, and it explicitly surfaces the ikhtilaf ('Some understood it as the sun's decline from its zenith; others connected it with sunset'), which is exactly al-Tabari's two-camp structure (ghurub, per Ibn Mas'ud/Ibn 'Abbas via Mujahid, vs. zawal, per Ibn 'Abbas via al-Sha'bi, Ibn 'Umar, Abu Barzah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Abu Ja'far, Qatadah; al-Tabari prefers zawal/Zuhr). Its summary that the arc gathers Zuhr-Asr-Maghrib-Isha matches al-Jalalayn and al-Muyassar verbatim in substance. Every attribution verified against the fetched tafsir: (a) 'Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir both read the verse in relation to the prescribed prayers' - confirmed, Ibn Kathir's heading is literally 'The Command to offer the Prayers at their appointed Times'; (b) 'Classical tafsir connects this witnessing with the angels of night and day' - confirmed in all four editions plus the Abu Hurayrah hadith in al-Bukhari cited by Ibn Kathir and al-Tabari; (c) 'the pronoun bihi is commonly read as referring to the Qur'an' - confirmed, al-Jalalayn glosses bihi as bi-l-Qur'an, al-Tabari 'fa-shar ba'da nawmatin ya Muhammad bi-l-Qur'an', al-Muyassar 'fa-qra' al-Qur'an'; (d) 'Classical tafsir overwhelmingly connects the maqam mahmud with... the station of intercession' - the word 'overwhelmingly' is earned, al-Tabari says 'aktharu ahl al-'ilm' and Ibn Kathir quotes Ibn Jarir's 'Most of the commentators said'. Morphology claims verified against the corpus: mashhud is PASS_PCPL (file calls it a passive participle), aqimi is form IV of q-w-m, tahajjad form V of h-j-d, yab'athaka from b-'-th, maqam from q-w-m, mahmud PASS_PCPL from h-m-d. The inline morphology comments use correct flat-segment indices (17:78:21 = mashhudan). Cross-references verified in the Uthmani text: 20:130 (before sunrise, before sunset, portions of the night, edges of the day), 11:114 (two ends of the day, near parts of the night, good deeds removing evil), 73:2-6 (stand the night except a little, measured recitation, stronger in imprint and more upright in speech) - all three accurate. Preceding-context claims verified against 17:73-77 (khalil offered for fabrication, 'lean even a little', expulsion from the land, the unchanging sunnah). No countable/absolute claims of the 'exactly N / only place / never / hapax' type appear anywhere in this file, and no truncated tafsir quotation - the file paraphrases rather than block-quotes. One optional enrichment for the human reviewer, not a defect: al-Tabari's preferred reading of 'nafilatan laka' (Ibn 'Abbas: night prayer was obligatory on the Prophet specifically) is stronger than the file's 'extra devotion... special rank', and he explicitly rejects Mujahid's expiation-based explanation that Ibn Kathir carries. The file does not contradict either view; it just stays general.

thesis: Allah details His signs not only to make guidance visible but to strip camouflage off the road of rebellion, so the servant refuses to let desire rule over revelation and surrenders judgment and its timing to Allah alone.

flags.quote: This includes decision, authority, final ruling.
flags.issue: Unqualified expansion of 'ini al-hukmu illa lillah' into 'authority' on the single most politically weaponized phrase in this surah, with no ikhtilaf note and no tadabbur/fatwa line. All four fetched tafsirs specify the referent narrowly as the decree over the punishment the mockers demanded be hastened: Ibn Kathir 'for the ruling of this is with Allah. If He wills, He will punish you soon in response to your wish! If He wills, He will give you respite'; al-Muyassar 'wa ma al-hukmu fi ta'akhkhuri dhalika illa ila Allah' (the ruling on the DELAY of that); al-Tabari 'ma al-hukmu fima tasta'jiluna bihi... illa Allah'; al-Jalalayn alone generalizes, and only as 'fi dhalika wa ghayrih'. 'Authority' is the hakimiyyah/Khawarij reading of this exact clause and the file supplies it without anchor or qualification. Compounded by the file's own translation, quoted twice, 'Legislation is not but for Allah.' - no fetched tafsir supports a legislative referent here, and al-Tabari in fact prefers the alternate qira'ah 'yaqdi al-haqq' (He DECIDES the truth) over 'yaqussu', which pushes the sense further toward judicial decree and away from legislation. This is a live adversarial-quotation risk on a pull-quotable line.

flags.quote: That is why the passage begins with *nufassilu al-ayat* and ends with *khayru al-fasilin*.
flags.issue: Imprecise inclusio claim. Verified against the corpus, root f-s-l occurs at 6:55 segment 6 (nufassilu, form II) and 6:57 segment 35 (al-fasilin, ACT_PCPL) - it does not occur in 6:58. But the file's own declared passage is 6:55-58, so the passage does not 'end' with khayru al-fasilin; 6:58 (wa Allahu a'lamu bi-al-zalimin) does. The bracket is real across 55-57; the sentence overstates its span.

notes: Thesis itself is sound and every other claim verifies - do not rewrite the file, the fix is surgical and local to section 4 of Part 1. Recommended fix: (1) add one sentence after 'Judgment belongs to none but Allah' naming what the mufassirun actually specify here - that the hukm in question is Allah's decree over whether and when the punishment they are demanding arrives (Ibn Kathir, al-Tabari, al-Muyassar all read it this way in context) - and drop or qualify the word 'authority', which is doing unanchored work; (2) either replace the Sahih International rendering 'Legislation is not but for Allah' with 'The decision/judgment is for none but Allah' in both the frontmatter translation and the bolded body block, or add a one-line note that 'legislation' is a translator's choice the classical tafsir of this ayah does not carry; (3) tighten the inclusio sentence to 'the argument begins with nufassilu al-ayat and turns on khayru al-fasilin' or scope it explicitly to 6:55-57. Optional strengthening: al-Tabari records a genuine qira'ah ikhtilaf on yaqussu/yaqdi (Hijaz+Madinah read yaqussu with sad per Ibn 'Abbas, citing 12:3; Kufa+Basra read yaqdi with dad, and al-Tabari prefers the latter because fasl between disputants is by qada' not qasas) - noting this would both add rigor and reinforce the corrective in (1). Verified and clean: nuhitu is PASS in the corpus (the file's 'Nuhitu is passive' is correct), nufassilu is f-s-l form II, ahwa' is h-w-y, bayyinah is b-y-n and al-Tabari glosses 'ala bayyinah exactly as the file does ('bayanin qad tabayyantuhu wa burhanin qad wadaha li'), 'ma tasta'jiluna bihi' = the torment in all four editions, and the file's reading of 6:58 ('If the matter were in his hand, it would be over') matches Ibn Kathir's gloss precisely - Ibn Kathir even raises and resolves the apparent tension with the Ta'if / Angel of the Mountains hadith, which the file could cite but does not need to. The file's inward turn on sabil al-mujrimin ('not inviting us merely to point outward... It is inviting us to become less vulnerable to the criminal path in ourselves') is good adab and defuses the takfir reading of that half of the passage - the hukm clause is the only place the adab slips. Metadata note, out of rubric scope: estimated_duration '45-55 minutes' is out of family for a 1560-word declared count (compare 3206 words / '27-37 minutes' in the Isra file).

thesis: Human footing on earth and the means of living inside it are both divinely made rather than self-achieved, so gratitude is simply truthfulness toward reality and the verse's rebuke names ingratitude as a misreading of one's own existence.
notes: Short, modest file that claims nothing it cannot carry. No countable or absolute claims of any kind, no tafsir attributions to verify (the file names no source), no quoted tafsir and therefore no truncation exposure, and the passage is not ahkam-bearing or contested. Every linguistic claim verifies: makkannakum is m-k-n form II in the corpus and the file's gloss 'settling, enabling, giving footing, making room to act' matches al-Tabari's 'watta'na lakum... qararan tastaqirruna fiha, wa mihadan tamtahidunaha, wa firashan taftarishunaha' and Ibn Kathir's 'made the earth a fixed place for dwelling'; ma'ayish is root '-y-sh and al-Tabari confirms 'al-ma'ayish: jam' ma'ishah' from 'ashta ta'ish, and the file's 'not narrowly about salary or market exchange... the means by which life is sustained' matches al-Tabari's 'ta'ishuna biha ayyama hayatikum, min mata'im wa mashariib'. The one reading that could have gone wrong goes right: 'It does not say you never give thanks at all. It says the proportion is painfully small' is the correct handling of qalilan ma - al-Jalalayn glosses the ma as 'li-ta'kid al-qillah' (emphasizing the fewness, not negating), and al-Tabari and al-Muyassar both render it 'your thanks is little', not 'you give none'. Passage-position claims verified in the Uthmani text: 7:8-9 are the scales/mawazin verses immediately before, and 7:11 opens the Adam-Iblis prostration sequence immediately after, so 'Coming right before the Adam-Iblis sequence, this ayah becomes a bridge' is exactly right. One thing the human reviewer may want to weigh, an omission rather than an error: al-Tabari attaches a sharper cause to the little gratitude - 'li-'ibadatikum ghayri, wa ittikhadhikum ilahan siwaya' (because you worship other than Me and take a god besides Me) - whereas the file psychologizes the failure as 'entitlement, distraction, complaint, or forgetfulness'. That softer framing is legitimate and the universalized address is grounded (al-Tabari and al-Muyassar both address 'ayyuha al-nas', al-Jalalayn 'ya bani Adam'), but adding one line tying ingratitude back to misdirected worship would put the file on al-Tabari's actual edge and would also strengthen its own bridge into the Iblis sequence, since Iblis's refusal is precisely misdirected worship-posture. Metadata note, out of rubric scope: declared word_count 1294 against roughly 785 actual body words. I checked whether this signals lost content by sampling 29 other codex-tadabbur-era files and the field is noisy corpus-wide there (deltas from -584 to +601), and the file's structure ends cleanly on a completed synthesis sentence, so this is metadata drift, not truncation.
